messages:
Jordan (Acme SRE): Hey team — we started seeing a bunch of 5xx errors from our users around 2026-03-15 22:12:47 UTC. Request id I have: req_44a1be5c. Can you pull server-side logs for that req_id and confirm root cause? High-severity for customer SLA.

Maya (Support): Thanks Jordan — can you paste the exact request_id (looks good), the exact UTC timestamp you saw, and whether this is hosted/dedicated? Also if you have a curl snippet that reproduces it, please paste.

Jordan (Acme SRE): Full details: req_id=req_44a1be5c, time=2026-03-15T22:12:47Z, region=us-west-2, on hosted (trial org). Repro curl below (redacted API key):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"open-xyz","input":"Summarize this...","stream":false}'
```
Sending sample payload and got HTTP 500 with body: `{\"error\":\"internal server error\", \"request_id\":\"req_44a1be5c\"}`

Maya (Support): Got it — I'll look up the logs now. Quick note: hosted trial orgs have 7-day hot retention, older logs get archived. Since this is only a few days old we should still have hot logs. I'll pull traces and loop in logs/infra.

Ella (Logs): Jumping in — internal search commands you can use if needed. We have a central log API and also Elasticsearch. Example queries:
```bash
# internal log API (auth required)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $LOGS_API_TOKEN" \n  "https://logs.internal.redwood/search?q=request_id:\"req_44a1be5c\"&from=2026-03-15T22:10:00Z&to=2026-03-15T22:20:00Z"

# OR directly query ES (kibana) style
request_id:\"req_44a1be5c\" AND timestamp:[2026-03-15T22:10:00Z TO 2026-03-15T22:20:00Z]
```
If you don't have internal creds I can pull a slice and paste the relevant lines here. Note hosted trial orgs: hot retention 7 days, cold archive starts at 7 days -> S3. We can fetch archive artifacts but that takes longer.

Ella (Logs): I ran the search on hot indices. Relevant snippet (sanitized):
```
2026-03-15T22:12:46.923Z ERROR [req_44a1be5c] model_forwarder: upstream error: connection reset by peer to 10.3.2.12:443, retrying
2026-03-15T22:12:47.103Z WARN  [req_44a1be5c] kv_cache: miss for prefix 0x7f, falling back to backend
2026-03-15T22:12:52.478Z ERROR [req_44a1be5c] inference_proxy: backend timeout after 5000ms -> returning 502 to client
```
Looks like a model backend connection reset + a subsequent backend timeout. Could be transient capacity/eviction on the model nodes.

Sam (eng-infra-oncall): I can also confirm from infra metrics — around that timestamp several model workers in us-west-2 hit OOM and restarted (OOM events from gpu-accelerator pool). I'm attaching a short archive of the host logs and pod events (presigned link, expires 1 hour): https://internal-artifacts.redwood/archives/req_44a1be5c_20260315.tar.gz

Jordan (Acme SRE): Got the tar.gz, thanks. I see the same OOM events in the pod logs. Any quick mitigations we can do on our side (we're on trial and using larger batch sizes)?

Ella (Logs): Two immediate suggestions: 1) try lowering your batch_size and max_tokens in the request to reduce memory pressure; 2) pin to a smaller model variant while we stabilize. Also we'll escalate to eng-runtime to investigate memory footprint regression on that model.

Maya (Support): I'm opening an internal ticket and tagging @eng-runtime and @eng-infra-oncall. Also Jordan — please upload a debug bundle (client-side) so we have the full cURL + request/response headers. If you want the exact command to create a debug bundle: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/support/debug-bundles \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -d '{"request_ids":["req_44a1be5c"], "notes":"trial org, OOMs around 22:12 UTC"}'
```
This will give us client headers, retries, and payloads.

Jordan (Acme SRE): Uploaded debug bundle (ID db_20260315_001). Also: we noticed a billing spike same time — token usage jumped ~3x for a short window. Filing a separate billing ticket but tagging you here for visibility.

Sam (eng-infra-oncall): For visibility — archived logs path (if we needed older history): s3://redwood-archives/us-west-2/2026/03/15/req_44a1be5c.tar.gz. Retrieval for archived objects requires approvals and can take up to 4 hours.

Maya (Support): Next steps: I assigned to eng-runtime to investigate model OOM/regression (HIGH). eng-infra will keep the infra artifact link active for 1h and can extend if you still need it. I'll follow up with a summary and expected ETA in the ticket (24-48h). Jordan, please confirm if you want us to pin a model variant or we can wait for runtime team analysis. :eyes: :thumbsup:

Jordan (Acme SRE): Please pin to the smaller variant for now and we'll lower batch_size. Thanks everyone, appreciate the fast turnaround.

Maya (Support): Great — closing this channel and continuing in the internal ticket. Will post updates here when eng-runtime has findings. :white_check_mark:
